children.name: Tail Risk Hedging
children.blurb: Tail risk hedging in portfolio construction covers the deliberate use of instruments and overlays to limit losses from rare, severe market moves, such as crashes, volatility spikes, or correlation breakdowns.

children.name: Sustainability Factors in Portfolios
children.blurb: Sustainability factors in portfolios are the environmental, social and governance characteristics of holdings that investors use alongside financial measures.

children.blurb: Pricing illiquid assets covers the valuation of holdings that do not trade on a public market, such as private equity, private credit, real estate, infrastructure, and stakes in private companies.

sections.body: Portfolio construction is the work of deciding what assets to hold, in what amounts, and how to adjust those holdings as goals, markets, and constraints change. Artificial intelligence enters this field through forecasting, optimization, natural language processing, and reinforcement learning, not as a single product but as a set of methods applied to allocation problems. In practice, AI systems now scan news, filings, and market data to estimate risk and return, then solve for weights under constraints such as liquidity, taxes, and client preferences. Personalised advice engines turn those estimates into model portfolios for individual accounts, often with automated rebalancing and tax management. Tail risk models try to measure the chance of extreme losses and to choose hedges that pay off when broad markets fall. Sustainability factors are folded into the same optimization, using scores built from company disclosures, third party ratings, and alternative data. Pricing illiquid assets uses comparable sales, cash flow models, and machine learning to estimate values where no daily market price exists.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts of portfolio construction are well established, such as mean variance optimization and simple index tracking, and AI has made these faster and more scalable. The harder problems remain unsolved, because return forecasts are noisy, correlations shift in crises, and models trained on past data can fail when markets change structure. Tail risk hedging is especially difficult because extreme events are rare, so backtests offer limited evidence and hedges can be costly to maintain. Sustainability factors are widely used but definitions vary, data coverage is uneven, and scores can reflect disclosure choices as much as real world impact. Pricing illiquid assets depends on sparse transactions and appraisal based estimates, which smooth volatility and hide true uncertainty. The honest limits are model risk, data quality, regime change, and the gap between a clean optimization and a messy market, and the site's tracking of 117 listed AI-related instruments with daily prices gives one concrete universe for testing some of these methods without representing the whole market.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: Each page under this section takes one piece of that pipeline and examines it in depth. Personalised Wealth Advice looks at how goals, risk tolerance, and tax situations are translated into automated portfolios for individual clients. Portfolio Optimisation Beyond Mean and Variance covers methods that add higher moments, transaction costs, constraints, and machine learning forecasts to the classic allocation problem. Tail Risk Hedging focuses on protecting against extreme market moves, including option strategies, volatility signals, and the limits of rare event modeling. Sustainability Factors in Portfolios examines how environmental, social, and governance data is scored, integrated, and challenged in allocation decisions. Pricing Illiquid Assets deals with private equity, real estate, and other holdings that lack daily prices, where valuation models must handle sparse data and appraisal smoothing. A reader can move from the broad advice layer to the optimization engine, then to the specific problems of tail risk, sustainability, and illiquid pricing, using each page for its own methods and open questions.
